conviction_note: The things that bear on this print are a negative read-through for the Q4 guide (Enphase's Q3 on Oct 27: European sell-through -12% QoQ, US resi -35% YoY, Q4 sell-through guided -10% and revenue far below consensus; Northland cut its SEDG Q4 estimate from $340m to $300m) against about 18% of float short and a +28.9% squeeze on last year's Q3 print. The negatives agree with a +23.9 put skew, so they are probably largely priced, and the stock sits 13% above its 52-week low. That leaves p_up 46 on an abs move of 14 (implied 12.84, raised because a Q4 guide is new information and the short is crowded). impact_sum -0.9 and the scaled -1.12 agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 revenue guide $310-340m (midpoint $325m), non-GAAP GM 22-26%, opex $86-91m, excluding IEEPA refunds (company 8-K Ex 99.1, 2026-08-05: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001419612/000117891326003833/exhibit_99-1.htm). Post-guide revenue consensus $330.5m (Benzinga EN) / $327.2m (Benzinga KR), https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SEDG/earnings-forecasts. The two roughly agree and sit just above the guide midpoint. A stale $377m Zacks figure predates the cut and is disregarded. Q4 consensus is about $319-343m (Benzinga) against Northland's $300m. The stock trades on the Q4 guide against that range. The Q2 print fell 30.5% on the Q3 guide despite beating on Q2.
positioning_check: Short interest 11.38M shares, 4.6 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (massive.com / curvedtrading, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/sedg/short-interest/), down from 11.9M on 9/15. Equibles put it at about 18.0% of float on 2026-08-19 (https://equibles.com/stocks/sedg/shortinterest). That is a crowded short, and the name squeezed +28.9% on the 2025-11-05 Q3 print. 25d skew is +23.9 vol points (downside paid), P/C OI 0.65, ATM IV 162%, event-implied move 12.84%. Spot $32.12 is -59% from the 52-week high and +12.8% from the low; run-up -5.6% over 20 days and -0.1% over 5. Sell-side is skewed negative (MarketBeat 'Reduce', 6 Sell / 13 Hold / 1 Buy; Citi Sell $30).

findings.finding: Enphase's Q3 2026 release (Oct 27, after SEDG last spoke) showed European sell-through -12% QoQ with France soft, US sell-through -35% YoY (+5% QoQ), Q3 revenue at the low end of its guide, and a Q4 guide of $225-255m against about $300.5m consensus that assumes sell-through -10% QoQ. This is a direct peer read-through on the two end markets (Europe resi, US resi) behind SEDG's Q4 guide, against a SEDG Q4 consensus of about $319-343m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SEDG trades on the guide. On 2026-08-05 a Q2 beat with a Q3 guide midpoint ~13% under consensus moved -30.5%. On 2026-05-06 the move was -9.0%. On 2025-11-05 a print with a positive outlook moved +28.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. SEDG has drifted -5.6% over 20 days to $32, and the skew is put-paid. But Benzinga's SEDG Q4 revenue consensus still sits at $319-343m, near Q2's $346m run-rate. If the street had fully passed through Enphase's -10% sell-through and Europe -12%, Q4 SEDG estimates would sit near or below $300m, where Northland already is.
findings.independence: Northland's Q4 cut (separate finding, a different source but the same theme) and Germany's September rooftop data (now.solar/pv magazine, 2026-10-16) both point the same way. Offset: SEDG said in Q2 that Europe was strong and US C&I offset US resi, and Enphase is micro-inverter with a different European mix (SEDG has larger C&I and storage exposure). This is net of those.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-30 Northland cut its SEDG Q4 2026 revenue estimate from $340m to $300m and its FY26 estimate from $1.33bn to $1.29bn, citing management's comments on the outlook for the final months of the year. It kept Q3 at the $310-340m guide. Its 2027 estimate of $1.34bn is about $110m under consensus. This implies a Q4 guide below the $319-343m Benzinga Q4 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide below consensus: -30.5% (2026-08-05). The stock fell after the Feb 2026 multi-year projections (-5.5% on the print).
findings.why_not_priced: A public sell-side note, so partly priced. But aggregated Q4 consensus ($319-343m per Benzinga) has not converged to $300m. If it had, a ~$300m guide would be neutral. A guide below $310m lands below most of the street.
findings.independence: Peer data (Enphase Q4 guide, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001463101/000146310126000101/a2026q3exx991pressrelease.htm) points the same way independently. The management remark Northland cites (likely from the 2026-09-10 investor day) is not itself sourced here.

findings.finding: German Marktstammdatenregister data for September 2026, published Oct 16, shows total additions of 1,226 MW against 1,644 MW in August, with 'the expected rooftop recovery has not materialized': residential rooftop up to 10 kW and commercial PV both declined, and balcony systems fell to 42 MW from 61 MW. Germany is a core European resi market for SEDG.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No SEDG-specific reaction history on German installation data. Europe strength was the support SEDG cited in its Q2 release.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry proxy that few US holders track. It is small because installation data lags sell-in, and SEDG's Europe strength in Q2 may be storage/C&I rather than small rooftop.
findings.independence: Proxy. Enphase's Europe sell-through -12% QoQ (separate source) agrees. The September total was still up YoY against 920 MW in September 2025.

findings.finding: Tigo Energy (MLPE peer) said on Aug 4 that the European recovery was progressing more gradually than expected, with residential declines in Italy and Czechia, and cut its FY26 revenue outlook to $100-110m.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it predates SEDG's own Q2 release and guide (Aug 5), which already reflected Europe conditions. Filed small for breadth. Tigo's Q3 lands Nov 4 at 16:30 ET, inside the window but after SEDG's print.
findings.independence: Enphase Europe sell-through (Oct 27) points the same way.

findings.finding: SMA Solar's H1 2026 Home & Business Solutions revenue rose 24.5% to EUR144.5m on higher order intake in Q2, and SMA said it expects improved HBS sales in H2. That is a European resi inverter peer guiding up for the half that contains SEDG's Q3 and Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific. SEDG cited strong Europe for Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since mid-August and probably priced. It offsets the Enphase Europe read. If the market weighted SMA over Enphase, SEDG would not trade near its 52-week low with puts bid.
findings.independence: Contradicted in direction by Enphase Europe -12% QoQ and the German rooftop data. Kept as the offsetting European evidence.

findings.finding: Positioning: 11.38M shares short (about 18% of float), 4.6 days to cover at the 9/30 settlement, with a put-paid skew of +23.9 and spot 13% above the 52-week low. SEDG's last Q3 print (2025-11-05) squeezed +28.9%, and 3 of the last 7 prints were double-digit up moves.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +28.9% (2025-11-05), +11.2% (2025-05-06), +16.0% (2025-02-19) on prints into heavy shorts. Against that, -30.5% (2026-08-05) shows shorts paid when the guide disappoints.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew prices downside. Any guide at or above ~$300m (the Northland bear number), together with a reported non-GAAP operating profit from the $11.5m IEEPA refund, gives the short side a reason to cover. That asymmetry is not in a put-bid surface.
findings.independence: Equibles shows 18.0% of float on 2026-08-19 (https://equibles.com/stocks/sedg/shortinterest). Baseline skew +23.9.

findings.finding: SEDG received $11.5m of IEEPA tariff refunds in July. They were excluded from the Q3 guide, but management said that including them the guide midpoint implies a Q3 non-GAAP operating profit. That is about +3.5 GM points on $325m of revenue, landing in the reported quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 included a $13.3m IEEPA benefit and a beat, and the stock fell 30.5% on the guide. The one-off did not protect the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed by the company, so it is mostly in the price. Some consensus GM/EPS figures may exclude it (Benzinga lists EPS estimates of a $0.04 profit or a -$0.23 loss, so sources disagree), which could make the headline EPS look like a beat. No path to the guide.
findings.independence: Same document as the bar. No other source.

outside_window.finding: Investor day (2026-09-10): $1.7bn of firm contracts for delivery through 2030, an 18% EBITDA margin target for 2029, and SST data-center volume deliveries from 2028. These are multi-year and do not resolve in the window beyond whatever Q4 guide colour is given.

baseline_tension: The negative peer read-through agrees with the +23.9 put skew and the -5.6% 20-day drift, so it is probably largely priced. The crowded short (~18% of float) and the history of up-squeezes cut against the skew, so p_up sits only slightly below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (negatives agree with a strong put skew, on a crowded ~18% short): shrank Enphase read-through -2.0 to -1.5, Northland -1.0 to -0.8, German rooftop -0.5 to -0.4; p_up from 45 to 46
Rule 2 (one-off with no path to the guide; Q2's IEEPA benefit did not stop a -30% move): IEEPA refund +0.3 to +0.2
Rule 6 checked: the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two roughly agreeing Benzinga consensus pages, so no cap was applied; investor-day items stay in outside_window
Rule 9: the Enphase finding is sized net of SEDG's US C&I and storage offsets, with no further change
